person.note:
See [BAQ9MH4T]: 193 for the main events of his life.
Three manuscript editions of his writings and translations were deposited respectively in rNgog Blo ldan shes rab's tomb, in the monastery of gSang phu (probably in the main assembly hall), and in Drin las kyi sde (ID:4357) ([7FZ3B926]: 107).

person.persName: zhang tshe spong chos kyi bla ma
zhang tshes spong chos kyi bla ma
tshes spong ba chos kyi bla ma
zhang tshe spong pa chos kyi bla ma
ne'u thog pa chos kyi bla ma
person.note: Third abbot of gSang phu ne'u thog monastery. Author of several commentaries, see [R894SIKE]: 405 (zhang tshe spong ba chos kyi bla mas kyang TI ka 'ga' re brtsams). Part of the group of the four main disciples of rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786) exX0032026-09-0202-25-28 .

Further holy places associated to him are: Ze thang, Grwa thang and rMog po ([647FFPZR]: 545, based on [Q3KCZX7B]: 38). Remembered for thirteen distinguished objects (such as royal insignia and religious articles), which could be objects of his clan ([4LDAV8UH]: 95.).

His dates can be approximated as 1070-1130.
He is possibly the same person as Byang 'chad khyung (ID:6382), as [NA9AMDH6] states that Khyung rin chen grags held Byang 'chad (ID:4416) and taught Sa chen (ID:4205) there ([647FFPZR]: 543). [CJ75QQKN]: 339 (fol. 8a/170a1-3). dMar ston's Zhib mo rdo rje ([RA3FK3BK]: 134 and 137), on the other hand, distinguish the two figures and places Sa chen's studies with Khyung at Nyang stod byang 'chad, and those with Khyung rin chen grags at Nyang stod.
On the reference to Khyung as "slang pa/slang pha/slang pha ba" (understood as a regionalism for "glang pa/glang pha ba," see [WL39GVT5]: 940.

person.persName: gangs pa she'u blo gros byang chub

person.note:
A funerary sa 'bum was erected in 'Ban grong to house his full body (see [647FFPZR]: 544, based on [Q3KCZX7B]: 43 and 92).
Possibly identical with "dge bshes gangs pa" alias Lum pa ba Ye shes byang chub (fl. late 11th and early 12th c.) ([CCSBSVCA] : 420, n. 25).
Expert in both scholastic and tantric traditions (exX0032026-04-2303-57-49 ).

person.note:
The majority of the information available on Phya pa has been provided in [EZ5JXHJY] and [8S7FDMCJ]. Summaries of the same are also found in [LQZU66YX]: 37-40, [F4UK2S8P]: 2-3, and [BW9UR427]: 35-36 (in French).
On his birth in 1109, the year of rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786)'s passing, see [TM8DW8WA]: 32-33, [VKBZTBWN]: 4b4-5, and [8GL7ZT7Y]: 15b2-3. On the date of his passing in a "sa mo glang" year, see [R894SIKE]: 400, [VKBZTBWN]: 4b4-5 and 6a5. [95UZA9Y5]: 40/3/5 (reported in [7FZ3B926]: 111 and [MPRU5QUC]: 206) specifies the day "sa mo glang gi lo'i nag pa zla ba nag po'i phyogs kyi tshes brgyad," i.e., on the 23rd of the third month.
A list of his students is provided in [EZ5JXHJY]: 356, based on [MQB8JGAX]: 297/4, [KL9XTQWI]: I, 454, [4YEPFBIB]: 340-341, [8GL7ZT7Y], fol. 15b3, [VKBZTBWN], fol. 4b7-5a4. [FDEWZ2NZ]: 290 also mentions the list of the four "jo sras" from bSod nams dpal's Bla ma rngog pa yab sras rim par byon pa’i rnam thar rin po che’i rgyan gyi phreng ba.
'Gos lo tsa ba lists numerous works composed before Phya pa took the see of gSang phu; these include commentaries and summaries on the Five works of Maitreya, the Pramāṇaviniścaya, the Satyadvayavibhaṅga, Madhyamakālaṃkāra, Madhyamakāloka, and Bodhicaryāvatāra. He mentions having seen these, the Yid kyi mun sel (ID:4503) and summaries on Madhyamaka, as well as (ID:4505) and (ID:5971). See exX0032026-04-2304-02-58 . 'Gos lo tsa ba does not mention any composition dealing with monastic discipline.
Śākya mchog ldan ([TM8DW8WA], 12-13 and 32) mentions a (doubtful) commentary on the Pramāṇavārttika (ID:3772) in addition to the commentary on the Pramāṇaviniścaya, and three summaries (small, intermediate, large), the intermediate one being the Yid kyi mun sel (ID:4503). (Discussed in [EZ5JXHJY]: 357, translated in [8S7FDMCJ]: 59).
Four groups of students are mentioned in Tibetan sources (which do not imply that the members of the respective groups were studying with Phya pa at the same time), with occasional variations:
1) The "Eight Great Lions" (seng chen brgyad). Eight scholars whose names contains the expression "seng ge," likely connoting their expertise in epistemology. The standard list includes gTsang nag pa (ID:3839), Dan 'bag (ID:3840), 'Bru sha (ID:3841), rMa bya (ID:3842), rTsags/rTsegs (ID:4289), Myang/Nyang bran (ID:3844), and gNyal pa/dMyal ma (ID:6679). The eighth one is instead sometimes said to be gTsang pa 'Jam dpal (ID:6336), 'U yug pa (ID:3846), or mTshur ston (DI:4315).
2) The "four sons of noble families" (jo sras mi bzhi) or the "three sons of noble families" (jo sras gsum). They are young noble men of the rNgog (ID:3847), 'Khon (ID:3848), Khu (ID:3849), and gNyos/sMyos (ID:3850). The four are listed in [VKBZTBWN]: 4a7 and [8GL7ZT7Y]: 15b3, whereas on 16a1 the author speaks of "jo sras gsum." The four are also listed by bSod nams dpal, see [FDEWZ2NZ]: 290.
3) The "three wise ones" (shes rab can mi gsum) or "four wise ones" (shes rab can mi bzhi). The threefold-list in [VKBZTBWN]: 5a1 has rKong po (ID:3852), lHo pa sgom gzan (ID:3853), Par bu ba/sPar phu ba (ID:3854). 'Gar dbang grub (ID:3851) is added in the fourfold list, e.g. in [R894SIKE]: 406.
4) The "three accomplished ones" (grub thob mi gsum). These are students who later became famous masters: Dus gsum mkhyen pa (ID:3855), Phag mo gru pa (ID:3856), gSal sto (ID:3857). The third is sometimes replaced by Zhang tshal (ID:6409), or is suggested to be the latter's direct student.

person.persName: shar chos pa dge bshes g.yor nyan
person.note:
Answering to 'Jig rten mgon po's (1143-1217) question about the best teachers in dBus, mGo zla pandita lists "g.Yor" along with "Phya" - Phya pa (ID:3831) - "Nyams" or "Nyang" - Nyang bran Chos kyi seng ge (ID:3844) or Chos kyi ye shes (ID:3876) - gTsang nag pa (ID:3839) and Dan bag pa (ID:3840) as examples of teachers of "mtshan nyid." ([7RUF6F47]: 78, n. 58)
The "dge bshes g.yor nyag" mentioned by rTa tshag Tshe dbang rgyal in his ecclesiastic history as a teacher of epistemology is probably the same person.

person.persName: khro phu lo tsA ba byams pa dpal
gnubs lo tsA ba byams pa'i dpal
person.note: [CTQMVBPR]: 37-38 an n. 40 reports that two dates are given in the [R894SIKE] for his birth: 1172 (given directly and can be inferred from the age given for him at the time of the birth of Chag lo (ID:6412) and 1173. [R894SIKE]: 828 sets his birth in a water female serpent year (1173), three years after the passing of Phag mo gru pa (ID:3856) (in 1170). Active as a translator, he invited the three Indian paṇḍitas Śrījagatamitrānanda, alias Mitrayogin, Buddhaśrījñāna (ID:5830), and Śākyaśrī (ID:6418) to Tibet ([2X2E3882]: 253).

bla ma la bstod pa (incipit)
g+hu ru sta ba
shAkya'i dge slong gzhon nu byang chub la bstod pa (colophon)
bibl.author: Anonymous
bibl.note:
Eulogy to the bla ma, following the text of the rGyal ba'i yum kyi bsdus pa'i don (ID:4516).
The colophon suggests that it is an eulogy to 'Jad gzhon nu byang chub (ID:3863) - the author of the text that precedes on the manuscript - by a disciple, but it could be possible that the colophon is mistaken and that it is an eulogy, by 'Jad pa to his own bla ma, an hypothesis that could find some support in the two-line annotation in smaller script that follows, which distinguishes a "bla ma" from Shag kya'i dge slong gzhon nu byang chub.

bibl.title: chos mngon pa kun las btus pa'i TIk+ka shes bya thams cad gsal bar byed pa'i sgron me
ཆོས་མངོན་པ་ཀུན་ལས་བཏུས་པའི་ཊཱིཀྐ་ཤེས་བྱ་ཐམས་ཅད་གསལ་བར་བྱེད་པའི་སྒྲོན་མེ
bibl.author: 'jad pa gzhon nu byang chub
bibl.note:
The work contains numerous named references to other scholars. The views of "'ban" ('ban dkon mchog rdo rje (ID:4243)) are frequently juxtaposed to those of "mchims," for whom we follow the identification of mChims brTson 'grus seng ge (ID:4261) in [MGPRHX73]. In the same way, the author frequently juxtaposes the views of "tho" (tho kun dga' rdo rje (ID:3921)) and those of "skyabs"/"byang chub skyabs" (ID:3864).
Portions of the work that are literally identical are found in mNgon pa kun las btus pa'i rgyan (ID:5268) by bTsun pa 'khon ston (ID:5865).

bibl.author: klong chen rab 'byams pa
'jad pa gzhon nu byang chub
bibl.note: The work is discussed in [FZ6N88AU], and [MGPRHX73] discusses its authorship, identifying the author as 'Jad pa gzhon nu byang chub (ID:3863), a student of 'Jad pa byang chub skyabs (ID:3864), himself a student of Phya pa (ID:3831). This epistemological summary is one of the best sources for the identification of the Tibetan interpreters referred to in epistemological works, as it names them explicitly (see [FZ6N88AU]: 415-416 for references).
